page: Microsoft Azure E2s_v6 is an x86_64 architecture virtual machine belonging to the Esv6 server family. It is configured with 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from a single physical Intel Xeon 8573C core running at 4.2 GHz. The processor features hyper-threading with two threads per core, a 260 MB L3 cache, and advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel AMX (Advanced Matrix Extensions). This instance is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. It does not include local storage or integrated GPUs, but it is premium storage capable.

Benchmark evaluations indicate a divergence between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The single-core performance is notable, with a Geekbench single-core score of 2149.0 and average ratings in single-threaded stress-ng, gzip compression, and bzip3 decompression. However, multi-core and memory bandwidth metrics are limited. The Geekbench multi-core score of 2641.0 and Passmark CPU score of 3745.49 are categorized as weak, while uncached memory read and write bandwidths are poor, measuring 21.51 GB/sec and 14.04 GB/sec respectively.

The primary tradeoff of the E2s_v6 lies in its high memory capacity relative to its limited processing core count. While the 16.0 GB RAM allocation provides qualitative cost efficiency for memory-bound workloads that do not require massive parallel processing, the 2 vCPU limit restricts its performance in multi-threaded tasks, software compilation, and database operations. This server is suited for lightweight memory-intensive applications, basic text processing, single-threaded data manipulation, and low-scale web serving where a larger memory footprint is required without the cost of additional CPU cores.
